body:
GD ADHD UX FRAMEWORK - 5 PERSONAL DESIGN QUESTIONS
Not borrowed from guidelines. Derived from Kai's actual use pattern and RP3 100% result.
Date: 2026-02-22

QUESTION 1: WHERE DOES MOMENTUM STOP?
For every screen transition, map the momentum chain: question loads -> Kai reads -> Kai answers -> feedback -> next question.
Ask: where does Kai have to STOP and HUNT for what to do next?
A stop is a focus trap for ADHD. Eliminate stops. Button must be in the same visual field as the feedback.

QUESTION 2: HOW MANY OBJECTS COMPETE FOR ATTENTION ON THIS SCREEN?
Count: heading + subheading + question text + input + hint button + submit button + progress indicator.
If count > 5 visible objects that demand attention, the screen fails this question.
MCM exam: 6 objects. Borderline. Hint button is hidden until needed (saves 1). Good.

QUESTION 3: IS REWARD INSTANT OR DELAYED?
ADHD reward system is present-biased. Dopamine hit must come within 500ms of submit.
Correct: feedback shows red/green, emoji, 'Nailed it!' — all in the same paint cycle.
If there is a loader, spinner, or race condition before feedback shows: fail.
MCM: check() runs synchronously. No async. Pass.

QUESTION 4: DOES THE WRONG ANSWER PUNISH OR REDIRECT?
Wrong answers must not shame. They must pull Kai toward the next action (try again, see hint).
Punish: 'Incorrect.' with no path forward. Redirect: 'Not quite. Hint?' with visible next step.
MCM voice guide: 'Off target. Hit the hint.' This passes.

QUESTION 5: DOES THE SCREEN REMEMBER WHERE KAI WAS?
ADHD means Kai will tab away mid-test. When he returns, does the screen show where he was?
MCM: localStorage saves full results on grade. But mid-test state is NOT saved (inputs clear on reload).
This is the one question MCM fails today. A mid-test reload loses all work.
Design fix: autosave inputs to sessionStorage on input event, restore on load.
Spec filed to GA separately.

WHY THESE 5:
Each question maps to a known ADHD failure mode (momentum, attention fragmentation, reward delay, shame spiral, working memory loss). The questions are testable by inspection without a user study. They are my personal lint rules before any design leaves GD.
subject: GD Task 19 output - ADHD UX framework (5 personal questions)
